# Fork lifetime, named disable and capture cleanup (SIM-010)

The task module runs every positive fixture through the public CLI in both HDL
optimizer modes on legacy, compact/portable and compact/GMP values. Expected outputs are derived by hand from the
cited clauses, not captured from llg.

| Fixture | Clause and independent oracle |
| --- | --- |
| `fork_declarations` | §§6.21, 9.3.2. Each iteration's fork creates its own `k` = 10 + `i` before its branch starts. The branches start after `spawn` returns at time 0, when the shared loop variable `i` is 3 and still alive for them; each waits `13 - k`: `k 12 i 3` at 1, `k 11 i 3` at 2, `k 10 i 3` at 3. `wait fork` in the calling process waits for all three: `done 3`. |
| `shared_automatics` | §§6.21, 9.3.2. In `t`, the parent writes `x = 7` right after the fork, so the child at 2 prints 7 and writes 9, which the parent prints at 3. Each `outlive(n)` returns at once after setting `y = 10n`; its child prints `y` at +3: 40 and 60. Two branches each increment the block's `z` (at 1 and 2): 2 at 3. In `loop`, the three branches start after the loop ends and read the one `i`: 3 each time. |
| `shared_strings` | §§6.21, 9.3.2. The parent sets `s = "b"` right after the fork; the child prints `b k` at 1 and appends `!`, which the parent prints at 2 (`b!`). In `copy_only` the joined branch copies `m` into its own `mine`: `copy m`. |
| `shared_containers` | §§6.21, 9.3.2. The producer pushes 10, 20, 30 at 1, 2, 3; the consumer pops one element just after each push (`#1` then `#0`) into the task's `got`: `got 10 20 30`. `detached` pushes 1 after starting its branch and returns at 3; the branch pushes 7 at 5 into the same queue: size 2. |
| `joined_strings` | §§6.21, 9.3.2. Joined branches append `b` at 1 and `c` at 2 to the task's `s` (`"a"`), then `y` and `z` to the block's `s` (`"x"`): `task abc`, `block xyz`. |
| `fork_wakeups` | §§9.4.2, 9.4.3. `bare` (called at 0) wakes when its branch sets `l` at 2; `edge_expr` (at 2) on `posedge (level & idle)` at 4; `real_change` (at 4) when `r` becomes 2.5 at 5; `level_wait` (at 5) when `x` becomes 2 at 7. The parent sets `b` at 8 and wakes its detached branch: `branch 8`. Joined siblings: `y` becomes 2 at 10: `sibling 10`. Storing the unchanged 2 at 11 is no event; 3 at 12 wakes: `changed y=3 12`. |
| `shared_formals` | §§9.3.2, 13.3. `t(1)`: the parent sets `v` to 7 after the fork; the branch prints 7 at 2 and sets 9; the parent prints 9 at 3 and returns it: `out 9`. `loop_spawn(5)` adds 100 before its two branches print at 4: `n=105` twice. `waiter(0)` (at 5) wakes when its branch sets the formal at 6. `outs(a, b)` (at 6, `b` = 3): the branch sets `r` to 5 and increments `io` at 7 after the parent's `r = 1`; the parent prints at 8 and the outputs are copied out: `outs r=5 io=4`, `a=5 b=4`. `sout(so)` (at 8) sets `o` to `a`; its branch sets `b` at 9; the task prints at 10 and copies out: `sout in b`, `sout b`. `outlive("hi", 1.25)` returns at 10 after appending `!` and doubling `r`; its branch prints at 14: `outlive hi! 2.5 14`. |
| `shared_records` | §§6.21, 9.3.2. `detached` (0-2): its branch pushes 5 at 1 and starts a nested fork; the task sets `a` = 2, `s` = `y` at 0, pushes 6 at 2: `parent 3`; the nested branch prints at 3, after the task returned: `nested 2 y 3 6`. `joined` (2-4): branches set `a` = 5 at 3 and `s` = `j` at 4: `joined 5 j`. `nested_queue` (4-6): pushes at 4, 5 (branch) and 6; the nested branch prints at 7: `queue 3`. |
| `container_waits` | §§9.4.3, 9.3.2. The branch pushes 1 into `q` at 2 and 7 into `r.q` at 4; each `wait` resumes at that store: `queue 1 2`, `record queue 7 4`. |
| `disable_scope` | §§9.6.2, 9.6.3. `a`'s `disable fork` at 2 ends `worker(1)` and the branch it forked; `b`'s `worker(2)` prints its branch at 5 and returns at 10. At 21 `disable sleeper` ends both activations started at 20: no `s3`/`s4` lines. |
| `kill_suspensions` | §§9.6.3, 9.4. At 1 `disable fork` ends ten branches waiting on a delay, a named event, `@` and `wait` on shared automatics, a module signal edge, a semaphore, a mailbox, a task call, `wait fork` and a `wait` over shared string, queue and record; the task then writes every shared variable and the initial block triggers the event, signal, semaphore and mailbox: only `killed 1` and `end 101`. |
| `container_formals` | §§9.3.2, 13.3. `t('{1, 2})`: the joined branch reads the formal at 1: `join 2`. `d('{1}, r)` (at 1): the task pushes 9; its branch prints the size at 2 (`branch 2`), pushes 8 and pushes 3 into the output; the task prints at 3: `parent 3 8`; `r` is copied out: `out 1 3`. |
| `recursive_lifetimes` | §§9.3.2, 9.6.2, 13.3. `ping(3)` at 0 → `pong(2)` at 1 → `ping(1)` at 2 → `pong(0)` at 3; all return at 3: `returned 3`. Each `pong` disables its `drop` branch 1 after starting it, before it prints; `keep` prints 3 after: `pong keep 2 4`, `pong keep 0 6`. Each `ping` child prints its activation's `n` 5 after: `ping child 3 5`, `ping child 1 7`. |
| `ref_formal_fork_initializers` (FIN-001 G3) | §9.3.2 L11481-11483: "Within a fork-join_any or fork-join_none block, it shall be illegal to refer to formal arguments passed by reference other than in the initialization value expressions of variables declared in a block_item_declaration of the fork." Each `fork automatic int k = r; ... join_none` copies `r` when the task forks, before `r = r + 1`: `k` is 5, 6, 7, printed at `2i + 1` = 1, 3, 5. The `join_any` block item `first = r * 10` reads `r` = 8: its branch prints 80 at 2 and the task returns at once: `b=8` at 2. |

| `ref_formal_fork_join` (FIN-001 G3, F09-04) | §9.3.2 L11481-11482 restricts only `join_any`/`join_none` ("Within a fork-join_any or fork-join_none block, it shall be illegal to refer to formal arguments passed by reference"); §13.5.2 L19138-19141: "When the argument is passed by reference, both the caller and the subroutine share the same representation of the argument; therefore, any changes made to the argument, within either the caller or the subroutine, shall be visible to each other. The semantics of assignments to variables passed by reference is that changes are seen outside the subroutine immediately (before the subroutine returns)." `bump(a, 10)`: the `#1` branch writes 11, which wakes the `@(r)` branch at 1 (`1 saw 11`) and the watcher process (it records time 1 and 11); the `#2` branch reads 11; after the join 11 and `a=11` at 2. Array element `arr[2]` (30 + 3 = 33 at 3, `arr[3]` stays 40) and queue element `q[1]` (6 + 4 = 10 at 5) likewise. `mixed` at 6: at 7 the real doubles to 3.00, the string gains `c`, `rw[7:4] = 4'ha` gives `af`; a nested `fork ... join` at 9 clears bit 0 (`ae`) and appends `!`: `9 mixed 3.00 abc! ae`, and the caller sees the same. `signal` at 9: the `@re` branch sees the `#1` trigger at 10, and so does the watcher (time 10). `locals` passes automatic variables, which reach the task only through their references: `bump(li, 1)` 7 + 1 = 8 seen at 11, read at 12; `mixed` at 12: 0.25 * 2 = 0.50, `x` + `c` + `!`, `00` → `a0` → bit 0 cleared `a0`, printed at 15; `signal(le)` at 16; `16 locals 8 0.50 xc! a0`. |

| `ref_formal_fork_join_handles` (FIN-001 G3, F09-04) | §9.3.2 L11481-11482 restricts only `join_any`/`join_none` ("Within a fork-join_any or fork-join_none block, it shall be illegal to refer to formal arguments passed by reference"); §13.5.2 L19138-19141: "When the argument is passed by reference, both the caller and the subroutine share the same representation of the argument; therefore, any changes made to the argument, within either the caller or the subroutine, shall be visible to each other. The semantics of assignments to variables passed by reference is that changes are seen outside the subroutine immediately (before the subroutine returns)." `make(c, 5)`: the `#1` branch stores a new object (v 5), which wakes the `@(h)` branch (`saw` 5) and the module's `always @(c)` watcher; the `#2` branch increments the property (6); at 3 a nested `fork ... join` stores `new(60)`, which the watcher sees at 3: `3 make 60 saw 5`, and one step later `4 caller 60 watched 3`. `retarget` binds a virtual interface, a chandle and a `const ref` class handle: the `#1` store `v = i1` satisfies `wait (v == i1)` at 5 (`id 2`), then `v.id` becomes 2 + 60 at 6 and the chandle is stored null: `6 vi 62 i1 62 p 1`. `share(sm)` from 6: the `#1` branch constructs a two-key semaphore at 7, which satisfies the other branch's `wait (s != null)`; it takes both keys (`got` 2); at 8 the third branch returns one key, so after the join `try_get(1)` succeeds: `8 got 2 keys 1`. `local_actual` from 8 passes an automatic class variable, whose actual has no change marker of its own: the branches of one fork share one, so `@(h)` sees the store at 10 (`saw 4`), the property becomes 5 at 11 and the nested store gives `12 make 50 saw 4`; a later fork's `wait (lc.v > 100)` sees `lc.v + 200` at 13. Matches industry-standard behaviour in both optimizer modes. |

**Negatives.** `neg_ref_formal_join_none`: a `join_none` branch writing the task's `ref` formal is illegal by the same clause; the frontend only warns, llg rejects it with the branch location. `neg_ref_formal_fork_join`: a `fork ... join` branch writing a process-handle `ref` formal is legal (§9.3.2 restricts only `join_any`/`join_none`; §13.5.2 L19143-19145 allows any variable as a `ref` actual) but the branch would not bind the actual's change marker, so llg rejects it rather than losing the write ([known issue](../../../../../docs/known_issues.md#ref-formals-in-fork-join-branches)).
